analysis.title: Morning Tidbits (Thursday, November 12, 2026)
key_insights: The MBA average 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.21% last week, a fourth straight weekly decline and the longest streak since Aug./Sept. 2025. Rates are still about 90 bps higher YTD and MBA applications are near their lowest level since Jan. 2025, so buyers remain on the sidelines.
Saudi Arabia produced 10.6 million barrels/day in October, up 27% MoM and 3% below pre-war levels, with pipeline shipments to the Red Sea stable. Gasoline prices have fallen below $4.00/gallon.

Two risks to Saudi supply remain: not all regional exporters can bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and Saudi exports are vulnerable to Houthi attacks, as September showed. The 12-month WTI target is $65/barrel and depends on a US-Iran deal.

Citi's US Economic Surprise Index is at its highest level since August 2023, while the Euro Zone's gauge turned negative for the first time since July. With a hawkish Fed, this lifted the US Dollar Index to its highest level since March 2025.
Raymond James expects fewer Fed rate hikes than markets anticipate and sees the dollar rally as possibly stretched. Stronger US growth supports its preference for US equities.
Anthropic's IPO is one week away, targeting a market cap of up to $1.5t, second only to SpaceX among IPOs. Reports say the offering is several times oversubscribed.

AI sentiment appears to be recovering from last week's post-election concerns, helped by upbeat earnings commentary. Raymond James stays positive on Tech, citing consensus 2027 EPS growth of 42% versus 16% for the S&P 500.

Artwork sales at Christie's, Sotheby's and Phillips rose nearly 70% YoY to $6.8b in 1H26, per Bank of America, the strongest start for the global auction market since 2022. Raymond James notes art values are heavily influenced by sentiment, like crypto and gold.

Previous close on 11/11: S&P 500 +1.3% (7,619), DJIA +0.5% (52,486), Nasdaq 100 +2.3% (28,374), Russell 2000 +0.9% (2,846). Futures were slightly lower at 07:35 ET. The 10-year yield was 4.99% and the USD Index 102.91 (+0.7%).
Today's calendar: Initial Jobless Claims at 8:30am (consensus 195.0K, prior 189.0K) and Existing Home Sales at 10:00am (consensus 3,800K, prior 3,990K).
